intro: Lesson 35. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: ءَامَنَ ٱلرَّسُولُ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ۚ كُلٌّ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتِهِۦ وَكُتُبِهِۦ وَرُسُلِهِۦ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍۢ مِّن رُّسُلِهِۦ ۚ وَقَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا ۖ غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ (٢٨٥)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers, [saying], "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say, "We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the [final] destination."

head: Word
Where

How to read it
rows: Madd munfasil, then ikhfa' (noon before ز)
Four or five counts; light hum
Idgham without ghunnah: noon into ر
Idgham with ghunnah: tanween into م

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Baqarah 2:285 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 2:285 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 2:285 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: List the four things the believers believe in (2:285).
questions.a: Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers.

questions.q: Why do Muslims not make any distinction between the messengers (2:285)?
questions.a: We believe in all of them as messengers of Allah.

questions.q: What do the believers say in 2:285?
questions.a: A) We hear and we obey. 2:285: 'We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord.'

questions.q: Al-Baqarah 2:285: «ءَامَنَ ٱلرَّسُولُ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: The last two ayat of Al-Baqarah are recited by many Muslims at night. Why might a Muslim want to end the day with them?
questions.a: They state our belief and ask Allah's forgiveness and help: a good way to end each day.
